title: Power Pages: OpenID Connect sign-in accepts encrypted ID tokens
summary: The roadmap description, automatic enablement and target dates are accurately reported, and the encrypted-token documentation gaps were confirmed. However, the table incorrectly reports no automation for existing provider configuration: Microsoft documents deploying site settings through PAC CLI. The checklist also names claims-mapping controls that the table should identify explicitly.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls table
claims.claim: OpenID Connect governance is under Manage > Products > Power Pages > Settings > Authentication > OpenID Connect > environment > Manage.
claims.quote:
In the left navigation pane, select Manage.
Under Products, select Power Pages.
Select the Settings tab.
Under Authentication, select the authentication option you want to manage.
Select an environment, and then select Manage.
claims.fix: Keep the operational path. Explain that after Manage the admin chooses site targeting, selects Continue, reviews affected sites and confirms Update. Note that the release-plan search excerpt at https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/release-plan/2025wave2/power-pages/manage-external-authentication-provider-governance instead gives Manage > Power Pages > Governance settings > Authentication providers; prefer the cited operational guidance.

claims.where: controls[1].api; Governance controls table
claims.claim: Automation for existing OpenID Connect provider configuration on a site is not documented.
claims.quote: With this feature, the Microsoft Power Platform CLI enables CI/CD (Continuous Integration/Continuous Deployment) of a Power Pages site configuration.
claims.fix: Replace the blanket automation gap with PAC CLI deployment of provider site settings. Microsoft lists adx_sitesetting as a supported table at https://learn.microsoft.com/power-pages/configure/power-platform-cli, and https://learn.microsoft.com/power-pages/security/authentication/openid-provider documents OpenID Connect configuration as site settings. Use kind pac-cli, call pac pages upload --path "<site-folder>" --modelVersion 2, docs https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/developer/cli/reference/pages#pac-pages-upload. Explain that this uploads prepared website configuration containing the provider settings, not an encryption-specific switch.
